reason: The transporter-bearing cell and arriving glucose and oxygen suggest the first step is getting fuel into the cell.
expectation: The cell will take in glucose for energy production.

effect: The transporter-bearing cell becomes the muscle fibre scaffold; fuel has not yet been incorporated.
reaction: I was surprised the cell first needed to be assembled into a fibre.
reason: Mitochondria use glucose and oxygen to support energy production, so these are a promising pair.
expectation: The mitochondria will process the fuel and oxygen toward making usable energy.

effect: Glucose is split in the cell fluid before the smaller fuel molecules enter the mitochondrion, where oxygen also arrives.
reaction: The picture clarified that the initial glucose-splitting step occurs outside the mitochondrion.
reason: ADP and phosphate are the components needed to make ATP, matching the goal of supplying usable energy.
expectation: The fuelled mitochondria will produce ATP from ADP and phosphate.

effect: The fuelled mitochondria produced an ATP supply, and the picture shows ADP and phosphate returning as ATP is used.
reaction: The return loop helped clarify that ATP is continually remade.
reason: The thin and thick filaments look like the complementary parts of the fibre’s pulling machinery.
expectation: The filaments will form a contractile assembly for the muscle fibre.

effect: The thin and thick filaments formed overlapping sliding filament units for the fibre.
reaction: The overlap makes their role in pulling clearer.
reason: The muscle fibre scaffold has spaces for its contractile units.
expectation: The sliding filament units will fit into the muscle fibre.

effect: The sliding filament units now fill the muscle fibre, providing its pulling machinery.
reaction: The assembly fits the scaffold as expected.
reason: The calcium pulse acts around the fibre’s filaments, so it appears to be the signal for a pull.
expectation: Calcium will activate the filament-filled fibre for contraction.

effect: The fibre needed an ATP supply before the calcium signal; ATP lets myosin release and reset while the binding site remains covered.
reaction: I was surprised that ATP preparation came before the calcium signal.
reason: The fibre is now ATP-ready, and the calcium pulse acts around its filaments.
expectation: Calcium will activate the prepared fibre for a pull.

effect: Calcium exposed grip sites, allowing the filaments to slide and the fibre to shorten without the filaments themselves shortening.
reaction: The distinction between the fibre shortening and its filaments sliding was helpful.
reason: The calcium-pumping membranes appear to return calcium to storage, allowing the fibre to relax.
expectation: Calcium will be pumped back into storage and the muscle fibre will relax.

effect: Calcium pumps use ATP to return calcium to storage, covering the grip sites and stopping the pull. The fibre relaxes under an outside pull and is ready to respond again.
reaction: I found it interesting that relaxation also requires cellular work.

mostWorthwhile.text: Activating the fibre with calcium was most worthwhile: the description connects exposed grip sites and myosin movement to the larger fibre shortening, while making clear that the filaments themselves slide rather than shorten.

leastWorthwhile.text: Fitting the sliding filament units into the fibre was predictable and added little explanation beyond assembling the parts.

surprise.text: I was surprised that ATP preparation came before the calcium signal. The result showed ATP helping myosin release and reset while the grip site remained covered.

arbitrary.text: The initial attempt to combine the transporter-bearing cell with glucose and oxygen felt uncertain: the game instead assembled it with muscle fibre structures. The scaffold makes sense afterward, although the reason fuel could not be combined with the cell was not clear.

continue.text: Yes. I would be interested to see how this fibre becomes part of a tissue and body system, although some intermediate assembly steps were less engaging than the explanations of how pulling and relaxation work.
